stem: A nurse is collecting blood cultures for a client with suspected bloodstream infection. Which action best reduces contamination risk during venipuncture?

options.A: Skip skin antisepsis to shorten the procedure because contamination risk is determined mainly by the culture bottle rather than the venipuncture site.
options.B: Disinfect the venipuncture site with an appropriate alcohol-containing skin antiseptic before collecting the blood culture specimen as directed.
options.C: Palpate the prepared venipuncture site repeatedly with an ungloved finger after antisepsis to confirm the vein immediately before needle insertion.
options.D: Collect every blood culture set through the same existing peripheral IV line because line draws are preferred over separate venipuncture sites.

rationale: CDC's March 31, 2026 adult blood-culture collection guidance directs staff to disinfect the venipuncture site with an appropriate alcohol-containing skin disinfectant before collection and to use a separate venipuncture site for the second set when possible. Therefore B is correct. A omits a core contamination-prevention step, C risks recontamination after antisepsis, and D incorrectly makes an existing line the default for every set.
educational_objective: Apply CDC aseptic collection practices that reduce adult blood-culture contamination.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_locator: Establish a blood culture collection SOP, steps 2 and 13: disinfect venipuncture site with an appropriate alcohol-containing skin disinfectant; use a separate venipuncture site for the second set.
source_claim_supported: Alcohol-containing skin antisepsis before venipuncture reduces contamination risk; separate venipuncture sites are recommended for separate sets.

source_original.stem: A nurse is collecting blood cultures for a client with suspected bloodstream infection. Which action best reduces contamination risk during venipuncture?

options.A: Skip skin antisepsis to shorten the procedure because contamination risk is determined mainly by the culture bottle rather than the venipuncture site.
options.B: Disinfect the venipuncture site with an appropriate alcohol-containing skin antiseptic before collecting the blood culture specimen as directed.
options.C: Palpate the prepared venipuncture site repeatedly with an ungloved finger after antisepsis to confirm the vein immediately before needle insertion.
options.D: Collect every blood culture set through the same existing peripheral IV line because line draws are preferred over separate venipuncture sites.

source_original.rationale: CDC recommends proper skin antisepsis before blood-culture venipuncture to reduce contamination. Option B is correct because it uses an appropriate alcohol-containing skin antiseptic before collection. Option A omits a core contamination-prevention step. Option C risks recontaminating the prepared site after antisepsis. Option D is incorrect because CDC recommends venipuncture and separate sites for sets when possible rather than defaulting every set to an existing peripheral line.
source_original.source_detail: CDC — Collect Adult Blood Culture Sets, collection procedure: identify the patient with unique identifiers; disinfect the venipuncture site using an appropriate alcohol-containing skin disinfectant and allow it to dry; disinfect bottle septa; collect separate sets from separate venipuncture sites when possible. CDC Preventing Adult Blood Culture Contamination guidance dated 2026-03-31; current federal guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: patient identification, specimen collection, asepsis, high-alert medication safeguards, fall prevention and communication that prevents safety events as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained original construct/key after verifying the current March 31, 2026 CDC collection SOP.

audit_findings.claim_audit: No unsupported antiseptic contact time or universal line-draw prohibition added.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only B directly reduces venipuncture contamination as asked.
